claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child. His name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about one child, Alex.

To help determine eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances better.

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 8 years old. He was born in March 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old and was born in March 2016.

**Are you Alex's parent or guardian, and do you have responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and I have responsibility for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

**Is Alex living with you in the UK as part of your household?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. That's important information.

**Are you currently receiving any other benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not currently receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

**What is your current residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another type of visa or immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen living here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

**Are there any circumstances where Alex is away from the UK for extended periods, such as living abroad or attending school outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't away from the UK at all. He lives here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

**Have you claimed Child Benefit for Alex before, or is this a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim. I haven't claimed Child Benefit for him before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to clarify one more thing:

**Are you aware of any reason why you might not be eligible for Child Benefit, such as having a very high income (over £50,000 per year) or any other circumstances that might affect eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have a high income or anything like that. Though I should mention - Alex has been in hospital for a while now, about 11 weeks. Does that affect anything?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for mentioning that important detail. I want to make sure I understand the situation correctly.

**While Alex has been in hospital for the 11 weeks, has he remained living with you as part of your household, or is he considered to be residing at the hospital during this time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been residing at the hospital during this time for his treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Do you expect Alex to return to living with you in your household once his hospital treatment is complete?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Once he's better, he'll come back home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that confirmation. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key details:
- Alex is 8 years old (born March 2016)
- You are his parent with responsibility for him
- You are a British citizen
- Alex is a British citizen
- Alex normally lives with you in the UK
- You are not receiving other means-tested benefits
- This is a new claim
- Alex is currently in hospital for treatment (11 weeks) but is expected to return home

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, a child can still qualify for Child Benefit even if they are temporarily absent from the household due to medical treatment or hospitalisation, provided they are expected to return to live with you. The key requirement is that the child is ordinarily resident with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- He is a British citizen
- He is ordinarily resident in the UK with you
- You are a British citizen and resident in the UK
- Alex's current hospitalisation is temporary and doesn't affect eligibility, as he remains ordinarily resident with you and will return home

You should be able to proceed with your new claim for Child Benefit. I'd recommend contacting HMRC or visiting the relevant government website to submit your application when you're ready.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
